Subject: Integration sprint ops playbook for Finex Systems

Hi Alice — great call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

What we heard (short):
- Primary integration: customer-facing chat + search; embeddings powering semantic search and a reranker.
- Languages: Python backend for service layer, some Go microservices planned.
- Auth: need API key rotation + KMS for key material; procurement will ask about key management.
- SLOs: typical request latency goal is sub-200ms for typical chat generation, with streaming for user-facing flows.
- Traffic shape: steady-state ~60 qps, expected peak bursts up to ~300 qps; concurrency peaks for generative requests estimated ~220 concurrent token streams.

Open technical questions for the deep-dive (please confirm ahead of the call):
1) Which SDK(s) do you want us to prioritize for the POC (Python, Go)?
2) Are you able to share a short sample of typical request/response lengths and any existing batching constraints?
3) Do you require structured/tool-calling output (e.g., JSON schema enforcement) or only free-text streaming?
4) Embeddings: initial index size estimate? (helps sizing comp + RAM)

Quick proposed next steps: 
- Can you share the traffic estimate spreadsheet (QPS x distribution x sequence length)? (attachment stub attached: finex_discovery_notes.pdf)
- Tech deep-dive (60 min): go over auth flow, SDK bootstrapping, routing by region/cost tier, and dedicated sizing. Suggested: Tue 10/27 or Wed 10/28 — what works for you?
- We'll produce a short ops playbook (autoscale policies, queueing defaults, concurrency caps) and a draft Dedicated sizing recommendation ahead of the meeting.

Attachments: finex_discovery_notes.pdf (notes from today's call)

Thanks — looking forward.

—Karthik

Thanks Karthik — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side before the deep-dive: 

1) SDKs: Please prioritize Python first (backend service) and Go second (edge microservice). We can do client-side JS later.
2) Auth/KMS: We require key rotation + central KMS (AWS KMS). Long-term we'll want HSM options for keys used in production. Can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed KMS in Private/Dedicated?
3) Traffic: attaching a quick spreadsheet with expected daily/peak QPS and median/99th token lengths (finex_traffic_estimates.xlsx). The peak hundred-second spikes are usually caused by batch ingest jobs (not user sessions).
4) Structured output: yes — we need tool-calling/structured JSON outputs for our transaction-extraction flow and strict schema validation on certain endpoints.
5) Embeddings: initial index will be ~8M vectors; we will run nearest-neighbor re-ranking for top-100 candidates.

On sizing and autoscale: we want to avoid cold-start latency for user-facing flows. Can Redwood present typical autoscale warm-up windows and queueing behavior (max inflight per model instance, retry/backoff behavior)? Also curious about how prefix/KV caching would apply for our chat sessions.

We'll confirm availability for the 10/27–10/28 window. Attaching the traffic sheet.

Best,
Alice Hughes
Head of Platform Engineering | Finex Systems
alice.hughes@finexsys.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Integration sprint ops playbook for Finex Systems — initial sizing notes

Folks — reviewed Alice's spreadsheet and sketched a first-pass sizing and ops playbook (see proposed_sizing.md). Highlights: 

- Dedicated capacity recommendation (POC): 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) with autoscale floor of 2 / ceiling 8 during ramp. This gives room for the 300 qps burst if we tune batching + streaming.
- Concurrency model: target 40 concurrent token streams per GPU for chat gen (configurable). For shorter inference lengths we can safely push concurrency higher but need to monitor tail latency.
- Queueing: suggest per-model queue with soft cap = 1.5x steady expected concurrency and hard cap to prevent OOM; Redwood runtime will apply backpressure and return 429s with recommended retry-after. We should propose a client-side concurrency limiter in the SDK (we have one in Python) to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Autoscale behavior: warm-up typically 60–90s for new instances to be ready at full throughput; can be improved with prewarmed pools in Dedicated (we can reserve warm nodes).
- Embeddings/reranker: embedding compute and vector store are separate; for 8M vectors recommend dedicated CPU/RAM nodes for index (or use customer's managed vector DB). Reranker calls should be routed to higher-throughput batch workers.

Open items for the deep-dive:
- Confirm whether Finex wants customer-managed KMS for API keys (affects Private vs Dedicated ops).
- Agree on P99 latency SLO and whether streaming tradeoffs are acceptable for cost.
- Determine whether we should enable KV prefix caching for sessions (helps reduce cost when users continue a session).

I'll drop the initial sizing doc in the shared Drive and prep a short slide for the deep-dive.

Attachments: proposed_sizing.md

—Marcus
